reading_note: The teaching unfolds the operation of love (fire) as it descends into the natural plane and performs five discrete works. Love is shown as that which (1) consumes and transforms whatever is offered to it, (2) discloses four discrete degrees of its presence — love itself, wisdom from love, falsity that obscures it, and the natural appearance — (3) imparts spiritual savor to whatever is prepared in it, (4) forms the vessels of doctrine that artisans of truth establish, and (5) manifests the light of wisdom by which men see. The arc moves from love's primary act (burning/transforming) through its differentiation, its quality-giving function, its formative power in doctrine, and finally to its illuminating operation — a complete circuit of love expressing itself in the natural cosmos.
